sentences.text:
The petitioner seeks that the judgment of this Court dated 31.10.2025 be reviewed because it has found certain facts incorrectly and has recorded certain dates in error.
2.

Dr.T.Jayan - petitioner appearing in person, submitted that the findings of this Court in the judgment relating to Ext.A4; and the testimony of PW2 relating to the building, are all incorrect and that he is, therefore, entitled to have it rectified.
3. He then pointed out that the further conclusions of this Court, that there were withdrawals from the Bank Statement on 21.08.2013; and the date of actual debt, are also in error.

4. Dr.T.Jayan, thereafter, submitted that the date of Ext.A11 recorded in paragraph 36 of the judgment as "10.01.2017" is wrong and it is actually 09.02.2020; and finally, that the case against him, filed by the respondent under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code (IPC), was filed after the filing of the Original Petitions and not before; and hence cannot be a ground R.P.Nos.4 & 17 of 2026 2026:KER:20563 of cruelty as has been incorrectly held in the judgment.

5. It is evident from the submissions of Dr.Jayan that, what he is attempting to do is to virtually seek that this Court rehear the Mat.Appeal, on the ground that we have concluded wrongly in our judgment.
It is needless to say that his remedy is not before this Court, but before other appropriate forum.

6. As regards the date of Ext.A11, even assuming that it is 09.02.2020 - as has been now asserted by the petitioner, it would be of no real consequence to the final conclusions, because admittedly, it is a solicitation for a second marriage by the petitioner at the time when the Original Petitions were pending, in which, he had taken the stand that a divorce cannot be granted.
In the afore reasons, these Review Petitions are dismissed.

Sd/-
